sections.label: THINKING
sections.content:
Big discovery! Clicking (57,6) — the end of the line — moved the purple square! The diff shows the square moved from (52-54,9-11) to (56-58,5-7). Then clicking (55,8) moved it further: to (54-56,7-9).
Wait, let me re-read:
- After clicking (57,6): the square moved from (52-54,9-11) to (56-58,5-7)?? The diff shows p→B at (52-54,9-11), and B→p at (56,5),(56,6),(56,7)... so the square moved from center (53,10) to around (57,6) — to the clicked dot! The square teleported to the clicked dot (57,6) (center (57,6), covering (56-58,5-7)).
- After clicking (17,46): only the timer changed. (17,46) is a dot near the ball... but the square didn't move there?! Hmm, wait, the diff for (17,46) shows only (63,52),(63,53) W→B (timer). So clicking (17,46) didn't move the square.
- After clicking (55,8): the square moved from (56-58,5-7) to (54-56,7-9) — to the clicked dot (55,8).
So: clicking a dot on the line teleports the square to that dot — but only some dots? (17,46) didn't work. (57,6) and (55,8) worked.
Difference: (17,46) is adjacent to the ball (the ball covers rows 11-19, columns 44-52; (17,46) is inside the ball's bounding box! The ball's blue extends to (17,46)? The ball's node 3 covers (11-19,44-52). (17,46) is inside the ball's bbox — probably a blue pixel, not a dot. Node 5 (G 1px) is at (17,46)... wait, node 5 is G at (17,17,46,46) — a gray dot at (17,46), adjacent to the ball. But in the image, the dot at (17,46) looks like it's touching the ball. Hmm, but clicking it did nothing (only the timer changed).
Maybe the rule is: the square can only move to dots within a certain distance of its current position? From (53,10): (57,6) is 4 rows down, 4 columns left — moved. From (57,6): (55,8) is 2 up, 2 right — moved. (17,46) from (57,6) is very far — didn't move.
Or: the square can only move along the line, one "step" at a time (2 rows, 2 columns)? (53,10)→(57,6) is 2 steps (53,10)→(55,8)→(57,6). That's 2 steps, not 1. Hmm.
Or: the square can only move to dots that are "downhill" (toward the bottom-left end)? (53,10)→(57,6) is downhill. (57,6)→(55,8) is uphill. So no.
Maybe the square can only move to dots within a radius of about 4? (53,10)→(57,6): distance 5.6. (57,6)→(55,8): distance 2.8. (57,6)→(17,46): distance 56.6 — too far.
Test: from the current position (55,8), try clicking (51,12) (2 up, 2 right) and (49,14) (4 up, 4 right), and also (45,18) (8 up, 8 right) to find the range. Also try (53,10) again (2 down, 2 left).
Actually, the rule might be: the square can only move to adjacent dots (1 step = 2,2). The (53,10)→(57,6) move is 2 steps... unless the square moves step by step, and the diff only shows the final state? No — each MOUSE action returns one frame; the square jumped directly from (53,10) to (57,6) in one action.
Hmm, wait, let me actually re-verify: before clicking (57,6), where was the square? After the previous turn's "square click" (53,10), the square was at (52-54,9-11). Then this turn: click (57,6) → square at (56-58,5-7). So it jumped 2 steps in one click.
Maybe the rule is: the square can only move to dots that are closer to the end of the line (57,6) than its current position? (53,10)→(57,6): closer to the end. (57,6)→(55,8): farther from the end. No.
Maybe the rule is: the square can only move to dots within a Chebyshev distance of 4? (53,10)→(57,6): max(4,4)=4 ✓. (57,6)→(55,8): 2 ✓. (57,6)→(17,46): 40 ✗. This fits!
So the square can "jump" to any dot within a distance of 4 (i.e., up to 2 steps along the line).
Goal: move the square along the line to the ball? The ball is at (11-19,44-52). The square needs to reach the ball — probably the dot (17,46) or (19,44), or the ball itself.
From the current position (55,8): the path is (53,10),(51,12),(49,14),(47,16),(45,18),(43,20),(41,22),(39,24),(37,26),(35,28),(33,30),(31,32),(29,34),(27,36),(25,38),(23,40),(21,42),(19,44),(17,46) — 19 dots. If the max jump is 2 steps (4,4), that's 10 clicks. If the max jump is 1 step, that's 19 clicks.
Let me test the range: from (55,8), click (49,14) (distance 6) — if it moves, the range is ≥3 steps; if not, the range is ≤2 steps. Then click (45,18) (distance 8)...
Actually, a better approach: test (49,14) first.
